101.headline: Ground floor, opening to the garden.
101.note: The quietest of the standard rooms — no corridor traffic past the door, and the garden terrace a few steps away.

102.headline: A corner room, with light on two sides.
102.note: Tall windows and a small balcony at the end of the first-floor corridor, with morning sun from the east.

103.headline: The city, framed and double-glazed.
103.note: Faces Gulshan Avenue, with glazing thick enough that the view is the only thing that reaches you. The guest lounge on this floor shares the same outlook.

201.headline: The corner suite, with the city at your window.
201.note: A full corner of the second floor, with windows on two aspects and a balcony looking out across the rooftops.

202.headline: Open water, from the moment you wake.
202.note: The bed faces the sea, and the balcony is deep enough to sit out on properly — coffee at sunrise is the point of this room.

301.headline: Quiet at the end of the corridor, facing the lake.
301.note: The farthest suite from the lift, with the garden below, the lake beyond it and the mountains behind — and nothing to hear at all.

302.headline: Wake to the water, on the quiet side.
302.note: Set away from the avenue entirely. At dusk the lake goes gold and the city disappears behind you.

401.headline: The longest view in the house.
401.note: Top floor, facing the water with the ridgeline behind it — the balcony is deep enough to eat breakfast on.

402.headline: High, quiet, and facing the ridgeline.
402.note: A window seat positioned for the morning, when the light comes up behind the mountains.
